title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22
source: Souree Info: Master Soundboard Reels > PCM > PCM (14-bit) (Sony L-750ESX-HFB tape); Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (wav 16-bit/44.1k)> Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac16; this source fixes the flaws in the three circulating Clugston sources: source ID 140868 and source ID 140892; this version includes a fix in track 11, Jack Straw

ai_review.summary: A superb marathon‑era 1973 composite with a fresh, crystal‑clear transfer, highlighted by an epic Truckin’→The Other One→Sugar Magnolia jam despite occasional matrix glitches.
ai_review.review: This release pulls together the best of the mid‑'73 marathon shows using a newly mastered matrix/composite that sounds remarkably clear, though a few left‑channel static spots and balance quirks persist. Musically the band delivers classic moments—Jack Straw, a killer China Cat Sunflower, a soaring Playing in the Band, and a massive Truckin’ → The Other One → Sugar Magnolia sequence—making it a must‑hear for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Three detailed reviews average to 4.33 stars, with strong praise for the performance and overall good recording quality despite some technical hiccups.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Composite of audience, monitor‑mix and Betty Board sources; occasional static/distortion in left channel of first set and poor balance on Bertha, but the new Uncle Chaz transfer is crisp and largely free of hiss.

standout_songs: Truckin' > The Other One > Sugar Magnolia
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑hour marathon with a relaxed pacing that builds into massive jam sequences; some sections feel a bit sparse, but the second set’s extended jams provide a cohesive climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Careful not to step on Bobby, pistons throughout Big River, starts GDtRFB riff in A, gives everything to Johnny B. Goode.
band_member_comments.Phil: Shows new ability to split pickups channels; engages in a wild Phil/Billy battle during the jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Delivers unique, soaring guitar work on China Cat Sunflower and strong contributions throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith excels on Race Is On, provides brilliant step‑into signature and stellar playing across the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy's ride/hi‑hat is prominent (sometimes too loud), his slow‑down section in Playing in the Band shines; overall drumming feels tighter than many ’73 shows.
